newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ARRESTS IN HUNGARY BOMB WAVE; MAYOR SAYS CITY TENSE.
newsitem.headline: ARRESTS IN HUNGARY BOMB WAVE; MAYOR SAYS CITY TENSE.

text.p: Hungarian police said on Friday they have arrested two suspects in a wave of gangland bombings and shootings that Budapest's mayor attributed to gang warfare.
"This is a war, this is definitely a gang war," Mayor Gabor Demszky told Reuters shortly before police announced the arrests of two men identified only as Peter S. and Laszlo R.

Police said that after arresting the two men on November 5, they confiscated handguns, 1,000 rounds of ammunition, seven hand grenades, 2.5 kgs (5.5 lb) of plastic explosive, silencers and a timing device during a search of a house used by Peter S.

"One of the handgrenades was of the same type as the one used in the bombing of the Leroy Country Pub on Wednesday," Colonel Janos Lazar of the Hungarian National Police told a news conference, referring to the latest handgrenade attack.
Since this summer, handgrenades set off late at night when few patrons are around have caused minor damage outside more than a dozen pubs, nightclubs and restaurants.
No bystanders have been injured, but the bombings have heightened tension in the city which is a popular tourist destination.
"There is a tension in the city because of this and everybody is waiting and demanding safer measures," Mayor Demszky said.
In addition, a known underworld boss, Jozsef Prisztas, was shot to death with a pistol at point-blank range as he sat in his jeep earlier this month.
Police also are investigating the shooting at Budapest's race track on Wednesday of one of the city's biggest horse owners.
Csaba Lakatos was shot three times with a rifle while he was walking in the stable area of the track between races and is recovering from his wounds in hospital, police said.
"We are presently questioning Lakatos in hospital," Lazar said.
Demszky said the violence could be linked to mob figures from neighbouring and nearby countries, such as Ukraine and Russia.
Police also have theorised that the underworld is in upheaval over the disappearance of a gangland "investment banker" who absconded with some three billion forints ($200 million).
